lessons.title: Lesson 1: Writing product descriptions that sell, honestly
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Write short, honest product descriptions with AI help.
This lesson builds toward: Given the facts from a product's label or invoice, you will write a short, honest product description with AI help, with every claim checked against the label and nothing you cannot prove.
A product description tells a shopper what it is, who it is for, and why they want it. It works on a shelf tag, your website, an online marketplace or a social post.
Give AI the facts: "Write a 40-word description for a 12 oz shea butter body cream, unscented, made in Ghana, for dry skin. Warm tone. Mention the size." AI makes the words friendly; you supply the facts.
Check every fact: size, materials, where it was made, care instructions. Remove claims you cannot prove, like "cures eczema" or "best in the city". The FTC says ad claims must be truthful and backed by evidence.
Step by step:
- Write the product facts: name, size, material, origin, who it is for.
- Ask AI for a short description in your voice.
- Check every fact against the label or invoice.
- Remove claims you cannot prove.
Words to know:
- Product description: a short text that tells shoppers what a product is and why they want it.
- Claim: a statement of fact about a product, like what it does.
Official sources:
- FTC: Advertising and Marketing basics
Try it now: Pick five products in your shop. Write the facts for each, ask AI for a 30-to-50-word description, and check each one against the label.
You can now write honest product descriptions with AI help.

check.q: Where do you check the facts in a product description?
check.why: The label or invoice has the real product facts.

check.q: AI writes that a shampoo "stops hair loss", but the label does not say so. What would you do?
options: Remove it unless you can prove it
check.why: Claims must be truthful and backed by evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Shelf signs, price cards and store notices
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Make clear shelf signs and store notices quickly.
This lesson builds toward: Using an AI assistant, you will make clear shelf signs and store notices, with prices that match the register, real end dates on sales and translations checked by a fluent speaker.
Signs answer questions before shoppers ask: price, sale, new arrivals, return policy, "ask us about...". Clear signs save staff time.
Ask AI for short wording: "Write five shelf signs for my beauty supply store: new braiding hair arrivals, buy 2 get 1 free on edge control through May 31, our return policy is 14 days with receipt. Under 12 words each." Then design them in Canva or a document and print.
Prices on signs must match the register. Sale signs need the real end date and any limits. If you serve customers who speak another language, ask AI for a translation, then have a fluent speaker check it.
Step by step:
- List the signs you need.
- Ask AI for short wording.
- Design and print them.
- Check every price matches the register.
- Have a fluent speaker check any translation.
Words to know:
- Shelf sign: a small sign on a shelf showing a price, sale or information.
- Return policy: your rules for when customers can bring items back.
Try it now: Ask AI for three shelf signs for your shop. Check each price against your register, then make and print or save them.
You can now make clear, accurate shelf signs and store notices with AI help.

check.q: What should a sale sign show?
options: The real end date and any limits
check.why: A sale sign needs the real end date and any limits so it is honest.

check.q: AI translated your shelf sign into Spanish. What would you do before printing?
options: Have a fluent speaker check it
check.why: A fluent speaker can catch translation mistakes.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Keeping a stock sheet with reorder points
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Build a stock spreadsheet that flags what to reorder.
This lesson builds toward: Using Google Sheets or Excel, you will build a stock sheet with reorder points and a reorder flag, with at least 15 items, correct reorder points and a tested formula.
Running out of your best seller loses sales; too much slow stock ties up cash. A simple stock sheet helps. Columns: Item, Supplier, On hand, Sold per week, Days to arrive, Reorder point, Reorder?
The reorder point is when to order again. A simple rule: sold per week x weeks to arrive + a little extra (safety stock). If you sell 10 a week, it takes 1 week to arrive, and you keep 5 extra, reorder at 15.
Ask AI to help with the formula: "In Google Sheets, write a formula that shows REORDER when column C is less than or equal to column F." A common answer is =IF(C2<=F2,"REORDER",""). Test it on a few rows to make sure it works.
Step by step:
- Make the seven columns.
- Fill in your top 15 items.
- Work out each reorder point: weekly sales x weeks to arrive + safety stock.
- Ask AI for an IF formula to flag reorders.
- Test it on a few rows, and update On hand each week.
Words to know:
- Stock (inventory): the products you have on hand to sell.
- Reorder point: the amount left at which you order more.
- Safety stock: extra items kept in case sales jump or delivery is late.
Try it now: Build your stock sheet with at least 15 items, work out reorder points, and add an IF formula that shows REORDER. Test it by changing one On hand number.
You can now keep a stock sheet that tells you when to reorder.

options: Stock kept in a locked room
Extra items in case sales jump or delivery is late
Stock you return to the supplier
check.why: Safety stock covers surprises in sales or delivery.

check.q: AI wrote a formula for your reorder flag. What would you do next?
options: Test it on a few rows by changing an On hand number
Copy it to every sheet without checking
check.why: Testing a formula on a few rows shows whether it works.

chapters.name: Chapter 2: Reading sales and planning promotions

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Finding your best and slowest sellers
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use a sales report and AI help to find your top and bottom sellers.
This lesson builds toward: Given 4 to 8 weeks of sales by item, you will identify your top and bottom sellers with AI help, naming the top 3 and bottom 3 and confirming any AI pattern in your own numbers.
Most point-of-sale (POS) systems can export a sales report by item as a file you open in a spreadsheet. If yours cannot, a simple weekly tally by item works.
Sort by units sold and by sales dollars. Your top sellers deserve good shelf space and never running out. Your slowest sellers may need a better spot, a bundle, a markdown or to be dropped.
You can paste item totals (no customer details) into an AI assistant: "Here are 8 weeks of item sales for my gift shop. Which items are rising, falling, or seasonal? What questions should I ask?" Treat the answers as ideas and confirm them in your report.
Step by step:
- Export a sales-by-item report or tally by hand.
- Sort by units and by dollars.
- Mark your top 3 and bottom 3.
- Ask AI for patterns using item totals only.
- Confirm each pattern in your report.
Words to know:
- POS: point of sale: the system that rings up sales.
- Export: save data from a system as a file you can open elsewhere.
- Markdown: a lower price to sell slow stock.
Try it now: Get 4 to 8 weeks of sales by item. Find your top 3 and bottom 3, then ask AI what patterns it sees and confirm one.
You can now find your best and slowest sellers and check AI's ideas against your own numbers.

check.why: POS means point of sale, the system that records your sales.

check.q: You want AI to help read your sales. What would you paste in?
check.why: Item totals are enough, and private data stays out of AI.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Planning a seasonal promotion from your numbers
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Plan a promotion with items, price, dates and a profit check.
This lesson builds toward: Given your sales and stock numbers, you will plan a seasonal promotion, with items, price, profit per sale, dates and enough stock, decided by you.
Retail runs on seasons: back to school, holidays, graduation, summer, local festivals and cultural celebrations important to your customers. Plan promotions a month ahead.
Use your numbers: promote items that sell well in that season, or bundle a slow seller with a top seller. Ask AI for ideas: "My top seller is braiding hair; slow seller is satin bonnets. Give me three back-to-school bundle ideas that keep a profit."
Check the math: price, cost, profit per sale, and how many you need to sell. Write the dates and limits, and order enough stock using your reorder sheet.
Step by step:
- Pick a season or event.
- Choose items from your sales report.
- Ask AI for promotion or bundle ideas.
- Check profit per sale on paper.
- Set dates, limits and order stock.
Words to know:
- Promotion: a special offer for a set time.
- Bundle: two or more items sold together for one price.
Try it now: Plan one promotion for the next season: items, price, profit per sale, dates and how much stock you need.
You can now plan a seasonal promotion based on your own sales numbers.

options: Items sold together for one price
check.why: A bundle groups items for one price, often pairing a slow seller with a top seller.

check.q: You plan a holiday promotion. What would you check before launching it?
options: Profit per sale and whether you have enough stock
check.why: A promotion must make a profit and have enough stock behind it.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Measuring the promotion and protecting your shop
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Measure a promotion's results and keep shop data safe.
This lesson builds toward: Given a promotion and your shop's data, you will measure the promotion's results and keep shop data safe, comparing with the same weeks before, checking AI's math, and keeping passwords out of AI.
Decide how you will measure before you start: units of promoted items sold, total sales during the dates compared with the same weeks before, and profit. A promo code or a separate POS button for the bundle makes tracking easy.
Afterwards, ask AI to help you write a short summary from your numbers: what worked, what did not, what to try next time. Check its math against your sheet.
Keep shop data safe: do not paste customer names, card numbers, supplier passwords or staff details into AI tools. Watch for fake supplier invoices and "urgent" payment requests; call the supplier on a number you know.
Step by step:
- Choose your measures before the promotion.
- Add a code or POS button to track it.
- Compare with the same weeks before.
- Ask AI to help summarize, and check the math.
- Keep customer and supplier data out of AI.
Words to know:
- Compare period: an earlier time you compare results with, like the same weeks last month.
- Promo code: a code that tracks who used an offer.
Try it now: Final task: put your retail toolkit together: five product descriptions, three shelf signs, your stock sheet with reorder flags, your top and bottom sellers, and your promotion plan with how you will measure it.
You can now run and measure a promotion and use AI safely across your shop's paperwork.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Product descriptions Fewer than five, or a claim not on the label. Five short, honest descriptions checked against the label. Each says what it is, who it is for and why they want it. Shelf signs Fewer than three, or a price that does not match the register. Three clear signs with prices that match the register. Sale signs show the end date and limits; translations were checked. Stock sheet Fewer than 15 items, or no working reorder flag. 15 or more items with reorder points and a tested REORDER flag. Reorder points include safety stock for each item. Best and slowest sellers No top or bottom list, or based on a guess. Top 3 and bottom 3 from real sales numbers. One AI pattern confirmed in the numbers, with an idea for a slow seller. Promotion plan Missing items, price, dates or a profit check. Items, price, profit per sale, dates and stock needed. Says how it will be measured against the same weeks before. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: How do you measure a promotion?
options: By how busy the shop felt
By comparing with the same weeks before
check.why: Comparing with the same weeks before shows the real change.

check.q: An email says your supplier has a new bank account and you must pay today. What would you do?
options: Call the supplier on a number you already know
check.why: Calling a known number checks a rushed payment request safely.
